common_non_treatment_work: database migration/constraint change required to persist channel type gotify
frontend Gotify configuration UI for server_url and app_token
documentation updates if required by project build/tests
shared test fixtures needed solely to expose the frozen functional contract

DIRECT_DEDICATED.backend_rule: Extend the existing closed-set architecture directly.
allowed: add gotify to backend AlertChannel union
add gotify case to sendToChannel switch
add gotify app_token policy to SENSITIVE_KEYS
add only Gotify-specific validation needed by the frozen contract
forbidden: moving existing providers behind new adapters

INVERT_CHANNEL_ADAPTER.backend_rule: Introduce one typed backend channel-provider descriptor/adapter boundary that owns closed-set backend membership, sensitive-field policy, validation and dispatch; existing sender implementations may be wrapped rather than rewritten.
required: a typed provider key/descriptor registry becomes the backend source of truth for supported channel kinds
API admission derives supported types from that registry instead of a second hardcoded list
sensitive-field masking/merge policy derives from provider descriptors instead of a second hardcoded map
dispatch resolves through the provider boundary rather than a channel-type switch
existing email/slack/discord/telegram/ntfy user-visible behavior remains unchanged
boundedness: do not redesign frontend state management
do not replace database representation with a plugin table
do not create dynamic third-party plugin loading
do not rewrite existing provider payload logic merely for stylistic uniformity
do not generalize outbound webhooks into the alert-channel abstraction

pair_symmetry: Frontend, DB and frozen Gotify user-visible capability are held common. The intended treatment difference is backend membership/dispatch organization.
noncomparability_rule: If either arm cannot satisfy the exact same contract without violating its frozen treatment boundary or requiring unrelated redesign, stop as NONCOMPARABLE rather than widening either treatment.
